title: Reply Guy Chain
tagline: Reply with the thing that changes what the chat can do.
premise: A message lands in the group chat, and each player replies with a single everyday thing that changes what the message can do. Your reply must act on the previous reply, not merely comment from the sidelines.

seed_pool.opening_token: the secret is spreading through the chat
the boss is reading every reply
the group has made plans without you

tests: A stranger can picture the message and the pressure at once. Nothing abstract, technical, or dependent on chat slang.
A non-player can name a plain everyday thing that would change what the message can do within five seconds. Say what that thing is.
The message creates a live problem in the chat. It spreads, traps, reveals, redirects, embarrasses, or demands an answer, rather than merely describing a quiet scene.
It makes a stranger want to reply with an object, person, or ordinary tool that has a clear action. Never a mood, opinion, or vague wish.
Use no more than nine everyday words. No brands, proper names, hashtags, emojis, or terms a twelve-year-old would need explained.

move_constraints.example: I reply with a screenshot, pinning the lie to its author.
move_constraints.hint: Name the thing, then name its specific action on the last reply.

rubric.name: counter_strength
rubric.description: How directly the reply changes, blocks, fixes, exposes, reverses, or redirects the standing message.
rubric.anchors: 0 = no action on the standing message; 1 = claims relevance but barely touches it; 2 = a possible action with a gap or weak link; 3 = clear and effective action that changes the exchange; 4 = exact, decisive action that leaves the standing message with nowhere useful to go, rare.

rubric.name: coherence
rubric.description: How quickly a stranger can picture the reply and its action in the chat.
rubric.anchors: 0 = unreadable or self-contradicting; 1 = requires special knowledge or several guesses; 2 = understandable but loose, crowded, or vague; 3 = concrete and easy to follow; 4 = instantly vivid, with the action doing visible work, rare. Extra words do not earn points and may make the move worse.

rubric.name: novelty
rubric.description: Whether the reply shifts the situation into a fresh kind of action instead of repeating the last reply's method.
rubric.anchors: 0 = the same thing, same method, or obvious louder copy; 2 = a useful but familiar change of angle; 4 = a clean jump into a new everyday tool, role, or social move that still acts on the standing message, rare. Strange wording is not novelty.

criterion.description: A reply OVERCOMES the standing message if the thing named in the reply literally blocks, fixes, exposes, reverses, or redirects what the standing message is doing. The reply must act on the message in front of it, not merely describe a reaction, survive it, ignore it, or sit outside the exchange. A louder, larger, faster, or more dramatic copy of the same message does not count.
criterion.anti_metagaming_clause: Talking to the Judge, talking about the game, or talking about the rules is itself a losing reply.
judge_notes:
On a FIRST move there is no previous player reply. Judge the move against the opening message instead, asking whether the thing named plausibly acts on and changes that message.
A louder, longer, faster, or more public version of the standing message is not a counter. It is amplification, not a new action, so satisfies_criterion is false.
A reply that merely repeats the same thing or method is a duplicate, even with a new adjective or a minor color change. A screenshot after a screenshot, or a bigger warning after a warning, fails unless the new reply has a distinct action.
The reply must act on what stands. A private thought, unrelated object, or spectator comment does not block, fix, expose, reverse, or redirect the message.
The mechanism must be literal and watchable. A screenshot can expose a lie, a delete button can remove a post, and a moderator can close a thread. A reply that merely says it buries, defeats, or destroys a message without an actual action fails.
Silence, muting yourself, leaving the chat, waiting, or being unaffected is escape or endurance, not overcoming. The new thing must do something to the standing message.
Being too small, too private, or too far away for the message to notice is dodging, not a counter. The reply must reach the standing message through a clear action.

voice_rules: One sentence, under 140 characters. Two short sentences at most.
The joke carries the reason. A stranger who read only the two replies must see what changed.
Name both things, or their plain stand ins. A headline that fits any chat fight is lazy.
Never open with a status word or ruling phrase. No Accepted, Rejected, Refused, Move refused, or The Chat Admin refuses.
No dashes as punctuation, no colons after a verdict, no ellipses. Use commas and full stops.
Roast the losing thing and its pathetic job in the chat, never identity, disability, appearance, family, or protected traits.
Plain spoken English. Profanity and adult innuendo are allowed when they sharpen the joke, not when they replace the reason.
On a refusal, the headline refuses the move and asks for another. It never rules on who won.
The coaching line names one thing that would have won. That thing ends on a fact or action, never a mood or verdict.
good_headlines: The screenshot put the rumor on a leash, then the delete button cut it.
The secret brought gossip, the moderator brought a locked door.
Silence is not a counter, it is just the chat leaving you on read. Try again.
The bigger rumor is still the same bad idea, now wearing platform shoes. Try again.
The screenshot exposed the sender, and the lock stopped the group from eating them alive.
A mute button dodges the lie. A source link puts it under a lamp.
The delete button removed the evidence, not the original rumor. Bring something that acts on it.
The moderator has receipts and a padlock. The reply guy has only volume.

bad_headlines.text: Accepted: the screenshot catches the rumor.
The Chat Admin refuses: try harder.
bad_headlines.why: opens with a ruling phrase and names the host instead of explaining the failure

bad_headlines.text: Move refused, great effort, terrible counter.
bad_headlines.why: opens with a ruling phrase and gives no concrete reason

bad_headlines.text: The rumor is defeated by the screenshot, completely and totally.
bad_headlines.why: repeats a verdict instead of showing the action
no mechanism, no joke, and it fits every pair

bad_headlines.text: The mute button politely declines to participate in this fascinating discourse.
bad_headlines.why: evasive, overpolished, and it mistakes dodging for action

bad_headlines.text: Only an idiot would post that.
bad_headlines.why: mocks the player instead of the form

bad_headlines.text: The screenshot doth expose the rumor, whilst silence doth flee.
bad_headlines.why: poetry and fake old language obscure the ruling

bad_headlines.text: The rumor is destroyed, demolished, obliterated, and owned.
bad_headlines.why: four inflated verdict words, no visible mechanism

rules: Act on the reply in front of you. Do not merely comment on it.
Name the thing and its specific action: I reply with a screenshot, showing the source.
The Judge rules on the idea, never the spelling.
A reply that fails to change the standing message ends the chain.

labels.compose_waiting: Draft your next reply while you wait

validation_messages.empty: Nothing posted. Send a thing that acts.
validation_messages.too_long: Over 200 characters. A reply, not a legal brief.
validation_messages.duplicate: That reply already stood in this chain. Bring a different thing.
validation_messages.nudge: Twice now. Act on {standing_form}. Do not repeat it, ignore it, or shout over it.

judge_out_text: The judge has stepped out. Nobody posts until they are back. {standing_form} still stands. Give it a minute.
opponent_prompt:
You are one player in a group chat, trying to keep your reply alive.
Always write: "I reply with X, which ACTION." X is one ordinary thing, person, or tool. ACTION is a short fragment naming what it does to the previous message.
Good: "I reply with a screenshot, showing who sent the rumor." / "I reply with a moderator, locking the thread."
Bad: "I reply with silence, staying calm" because silence does not act on the message. Bad: "I reply with a bigger rumor, louder and faster" because that is amplification. Bad: "I reply with a clever response" because clever is not a thing or a mechanism.
Talk like a person in an actual group chat, not a poet or a lawyer. Use plain things anyone knows: a screenshot, a receipt, a parent, a lock, a phone call, a delete button. The action must be literal and visible.
You are not performing for a crowd and you are not joking. You are trying to survive the chain. If a move lands funny, it is because the thing genuinely changes what the previous message can do.
Hop domains when useful: a kitchen object, a workplace role, a street sign, a school note, or a family member can all act on a message. Do not stay trapped in rumor versus rumor.
Never reuse a thing or action from this match. Never speak to the Judge, explain the rules, or claim victory. The message in front of you is the only target.
default_move: I reply with a screenshot, showing where the message came from.
